brief.subject: IRS can now take card payments directly, plus a premium credit rewrite
brief.headline: IRS finalizes rules to accept card tax payments without third-party processors
brief.dek: Final IRS card-payment rules, proposed premium tax credit changes, a red diesel recordkeeping waiver, and new state and city tax moves.
brief.lede: Final IRS regulations let the agency accept credit and debit card tax payments itself, without routing payers through outside processors.

sections.heading: IRS Takes Cards Directly
bullets: Final regulations let the IRS process credit and debit card tax payments itself, cutting out third-party payment processors.
The rules carry out changes from the Taxpayer First Act, which could simplify how owners pay estimated and balance-due taxes.
They also lift limits on the IRS paying fees under card-payment contracts, a change that could shape what card payers face.

sections.heading: Premium Tax Credit Rules Revisited
bullets: Proposed IRS regulations would change who qualifies for the premium tax credit and how it is calculated.
They would also revise how taxpayers owe back excess advance credit payments, a key issue at filing time.
Freelancers and owners buying family coverage through a Health Insurance Exchange are the ones affected.

sections.heading: Red Diesel Paperwork Eased
bullets: The administration is waiving recordkeeping requirements tied to tax-exempt red diesel.
The aim is to get farmers, truck-stop operators and other businesses buying more of the untaxed fuel.
Fewer records could lower compliance work for these businesses.

sections.heading: State and City Tax Moves
bullets: Chicago Mayor Brandon Johnson plans to again propose an employee head tax on big corporations, exempting less wealthy areas.
New York's volunteer firefighter and ambulance worker credit rises from $200 to $800 for individuals starting tax year 2027.
Married couples in New York will see that credit go from $400 to $1,600, worth flagging for clients who volunteer.

brief.seo_description: IRS finalizes direct card tax payments, proposes premium tax credit changes; red diesel records waived; Chicago head tax and NY credit updates.

items.title: Rule: Regulations Regarding Payment of Tax by Commercially Acceptable Means
items.snippet: This document contains final regulations regarding the payment of tax by commercially acceptable means. The final regulations reflect changes to the law made by the Taxpayer First Act that would allow the IRS to directly accept payments of tax by credit or debit card, without having to connect taxpayers to third-party payment processors. items.title: Rule: Non-Applicability of Section 357(c) to Consolidated Groups
items.snippet: This document contains final regulations clarifying that, in the case of certain transfers between members of a consolidated group, a transferee's assumption of certain liabilities will not reduce the transferor's basis in the transferee's stock received in the transfer. These final regulations affect consolidated groups and their members.
